title: SAP S/4Hana Key User / Fachbereichskoordinator
description: SAP S/4HANA Fachbereichskoordinator (m/w/d) Über uns Wir sehen die Halbleiterindustrie als Raum voller Möglichkeiten. Wir sehen Chancen. Und wir sehen das enorme Potenzial unserer Graphenlösungen, die Branche grundlegend zu verändern. Wir laden dich ein, diesen Wandel mitzugestalten und mit unserem konsequent menschenorientierten Ansatz kluge Köpfe für eine gemeinsame Vision zu vereinen. Unsere Vision: Zeige allen, dass du grundlegende Veränderungen bewirken kannst. Beweise mit deinem Wissen und deinen Fähigkeiten, dass Dinge auch anders gemacht werden können. Gemeinsam verändern wir die Art und Weise, wie die Welt miteinander verbunden ist. Über unsere Technologie Die Halbleiterindustrie benötigt zunehmend leistungsfähigere Chips mit höherer Bandbreite und geringerem Energieverbrauch. Unsere Technologie bietet dafür eine Lösung: Wir verbinden Chips zu leistungsstarken Computernetzwerken mit hohem Datendurchsatz und geringer Latenz. Der Schlüssel liegt in den besonderen physikalischen Eigenschaften von Graphen. Sie ermöglichen es uns, elektronische Datenverarbeitung mit photonischer Kommunikation zu verbinden, sodass unzählige Chips nahezu so miteinander interagieren können, als wären sie ein einziger. Unsere Innovation im Bereich der Graphenphotonik hebt Rechenleistung und Energieeffizienz auf ein völlig neues Niveau. Kurz gesagt: Wir verbinden Chips zu leistungsstarken und energieeffizienten Netzwerken und überwinden damit bestehende Grenzen der Konnektivität in der Halbleiterindustrie. Wir liefern die Graphenlösung. Deine Rolle Die Black Semiconductor GmbH sucht einen SAP S/4HANA Fachbereichskoordinator (m/w/d) , der als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen den Fachbereichen und externen SAP-Beratern agiert und sicherstellt, dass geschäftliche Anforderungen effektiv in geeignete Systemlösungen übersetzt werden. description: About the role Gauss Fusion is aiming to build the first commercial scale fusion power plant based on the stellarator concept and is seeking an experienced mechanical engineer to lead on development of the robotic maintenance approach. The fusion environment within the reactor is very aggressive, and in-vessel components such as the breeder blanket and divertor will need to be replaced on a regular basis as the materials become damaged by the radiation. Due to the environment inside the device, and in order to maintain a high overall availability, the maintenance must be done robotically using automated systems to extract and replace the components and bring the removed ones to a hot cell for separation, waste treatment, and recycling. Gauss Fusion is looking for an innovative mechanical design engineer with experience in robotics to lead the work defining and developing the maintenance approach for the Gauss stellarator power plant and its key stellarator systems. While the magnetic configuration will be designed to maximise access to the reactor, the complex geometry poses a challenge to fixations and kinematics, and inventive approaches to the problem are required. Main responsibilities Manage the Gauss Fusion maintenance approach to meet the requirements of a commercial scale fusion power plant design: Develop workable approaches to achieving high power plant availability, taking account of engineering and physics requirements across the reactor. Integrate these remote maintenance requirements into plant layout specifications. Define approaches to minimising hot cell inventory through efficient handling of removed components. Lead development of the breeder blanket and divertor segmentation and fixations resulting from these approaches. Lead development of remote maintenance testing and demonstration systems for the reactor. Qualification and educational requirements Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field, master’s or Ph.D. preferred. Technical experience: Minimum of 6 years of experience in mechanical engineering, preferably in large-scale engineering projects. Experience in designing complex mechanical systems, preferably in the energy or nuclear industry. Familiarity with CAD software and engineering analysis tools. Competences and preferred skills Experience developing remote maintenance systems operating in hazardous environments Strong background in mechatronics, motion control and mechanical integration. Experience with digital mock-up will be an asset Familiarity with maintenance, inspection and intervention systems Familiarity with system engineering processes, requirements management and verification activities. Strong understanding of mechanical design principles and engineering mechanics. Proficiency in structural analysis, finite element analysis (FEA), and kinematic analysis. Ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and coordinate with other engineering disciplines. Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Full time paid Internship DSU/ Stage DSU Paris
description: Introduction The selected person will join the Technopolis Group Data Science Unit (DSU), whose members work across different country offices. Our growing team brings together diverse academic backgrounds and a shared passion for developing data science applications to improve policymaking. The DSU contributes to policy consulting projects and conducts R&D to develop and test new applications, sometimes in collaboration with internal and external partners. Its work includes record linkage, classification, natural language processing, web scraping, generative AI and dynamic visualisations. As an intern, you will work alongside experienced data scientists and policy consultants, applying and developing your technical skills to address real-world policy questions. About this job The role of the intern in data science for public policy will be to support the data science components of policy evaluations , sectoral studies and strategic consultancy projects. Our clients include French regional councils, the French Development Agency (AFD), ADEME, the European Commission and multilateral development banks. You will be part of the DSU and collaborate with colleagues across policy areas, including science, technology and innovation, economic development, the green transition, international cooperation and health. You may also contribute to internal R&D and business development activities, particularly the preparation of data science approaches for project proposals. No previous professional experience is required. Relevant coursework, academic research and personal coding projects will be considered. We are looking to recruit a full-time intern for at least 6 months starting in Automn 2026 . Internship should be sponsored by the intern’s university (stage conventionné). Your profile We are looking for a curious and motivated individual who enjoys working with data and wants to understand how data science can inform public policy. Suitable candidates should have: Master’s-level studies in data science, computer science, statistics, economics, engineering or another relevant discipline with a strong quantitative component, and be eligible for a university-sponsored internship. Practical programming skills in Python, demonstrated through coursework, research or personal projects, and the ability to write and understand their own analytical code. Good foundations in statistics and quantitative analysis, together with an interest in economics and public policy and in interpreting analytical results in their policy context. Basic familiarity with machine learning or natural language processing, and an interest in using generative AI and large language models programmatically through APIs for data processing, text analysis and knowledge extraction. A careful and structured approach to working with data, including attention to data quality, validation, documentation and reproducibility. An interest in public policy and in using data science to support evidence-based policymaking , particularly in areas such as science, technology and innovation, economic development, the green transition or health policy. Fluency in French and English, good communication skills and an ability to work collaboratively in an international and multicultural environment. A third language would be an asset. Your responsibilities Working under the guidance of experienced colleagues, you will: Support the design and implementation of data science analyses to answer policy questions, writing code in Python. Collect, clean, link and validate data from multiple sources, including open datasets, databases and web-based sources. Help develop and test analytical workflows, potentially involving machine learning, NLP and LLM APIs for classification, text analysis and knowledge extraction. Contribute to indicators, scoreboards and visualisations, including dashboards where relevant, to make findings accessible to different audiences. Interpret and communicate results, helping prepare reports, methodological documentation and presentations for clients. Contribute to the DSU’s R&D and proposal preparation, for example by exploring new datasets, testing methods or developing small prototypes. Our offer We offer a paid internship in Paris, with hands-on experience at the intersection of data science and public policy. You will work with an international, multidisciplinary team, receive guidance from experienced colleagues and contribute to both client projects and the development of new analytical applications. Many of our interns become full-time staff at Technopolis or go on to pursue opportunities in the public and private sectors. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Design Release Engineer -Airframe
description: About Us Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces. Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected. The Role We are looking for a Senior Design Release Manager to join our Airframe Team in Lausanne. In this role, you will bridge the gap between initial mechanical concept and full-scale manufacturing, taking complete ownership of the manufacturing dossier for our composite structures and airframe modules. From day one, you will drive Design for Manufacturability and Design for Assembly directly inside the design loop, before parts are frozen. You will set and hold the release standard, define geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, manage engineering change orders, and act as the single authority signing off on product transfer gates to manufacturing. What You Will Do Manufacturing Dossier Ownership: Own and maintain the complete transfer package for your designated airframe module, including controlled drawing packages, bill of materials structures, material and finish specifications, critical characteristics, and acceptance criteria. Design Loop Integration: Collaborate directly with mechanical design engineers early in the design phase to optimize composite layups, bonded joints, tooling interfaces, and tolerance stack-ups while design changes are still fast and low cost. Transfer Gate & Release Authority: Serve as the final authority on product release packages, evaluating transfer readiness against gate standards before handing hardware over to manufacturing operations. Disposition & Configuration Management: Manage engineering change orders and serve as the single technical contact for drawing dispositions, non-conformance reviews, and design clarification requests from the production line. Supplier & Manufacturing Alignment: Work closely with production operations and external suppliers to evaluate manufacturing constraints for composite structures and precision assemblies. Feedback & Continuous Improvement: Analyze initial production build data and floor feedback to refine manufacturing dossiers and update gate standards for future design iterations. What We Are Looking For Background: B.Sc . or M.Sc . in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline. Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerance Analysis: Practical mastery of applying GD&T with intent, performing tolerance stack-up analyses, and defining clear acceptance criteria. Composite Structures & Manufacturing: Strong working knowledge of composite materials, layup sequences, tooling limitations, cure cycles, and bonded structural joints. Drawing & Package Control: Proven experience owning released drawing packages, managing structured bill of materials, and running engineering change order workflows. Early Stage Execution: Demonstrated success integrating manufacturing and assembly principles directly into active design reviews rather than conducting post-design audits. Language Skills: Professional proficiency in both English and French to work fluidly across design engineering and French-speaking production teams. What We Offer Direct ownership in defining the release and manufacturing transfer standards for high-performance defense airframes. Active collaboration with design engineers early in the development cycle where engineering decisions carry high leverage. High-visibility technical impact across fast-scaling, hardware-centric production programs. We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI. title: Characterization Lead
description: At Kandou , we are redeﬁning the economics of AI infrastructure. Our mission is to democratise AI by signiﬁcantly reducing the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) of hardware systems — a critical barrier to scalable adoption. Our proprietary MIMO-over-copper technology powers a high-performance, chiplet-based AI memory fabric that is both scalable and energy-efficient . Unlike traditional interconnects, our solution reduces power consumption signiﬁcantly while preserving high bandwidth and ultra-low latency — unlocking unprecedented efficiency for AI training and inference at scale. As Characterization Lead, you will own performance characterization of Zinal retimer silicon and the Randa Active Electrical Cable (AEC) channel. This is a Principal / Senior Staff individual contributor role with hands-on technical leadership. Your measurements will establish datasheet limits, channel classes and guard-bands for validation, manufacturing and customer specifications. Based primarily in Lausanne, you will work with silicon, signal integrity and validation teams, including channel characterization partners in Taiwan. Responsabilities · Lead silicon and channel characterization from measurement planning and bench setup through analysis, limit derivation and documented hand-off to validation. · Characterize TX/RX SerDes performance across process, voltage and temperature: swing, jitter, sensitivity, equalization, adaptation, CDR lock, BER bathtubs and shmoos. · Own channel measurements to at least 50 GHz, including de-embedding, insertion/return loss, mixed-mode S-parameters and common-mode and mode-conversion behavior. · Establish reference-paddle baselines and channel classes by gauge, reach and frequency; correlate HTDR-derived metrics with calibrated VNA measurements. · Derive datasheet limits and guard-bands from measured distributions, accounting for uncertainty, sample coverage and aging; maintain traceable datasets and limit revisions. · Assess carrier-loading and forwarded-clock tradeoffs using measured channel data and simulation, and translate the findings into supported configurations and characterization limits. · Characterize power, energy per bit and thermal behavior across operating modes and corners; investigate equalizer noise amplification and channel/thermal interactions. · Coordinate shared laboratory equipment and characterization milestones with validation teams; lead technical reviews and deliver limits in time for downstream qualification and screening. Essential Experience · 10 to 14 years of experience in SerDes/silicon characterization and/or high-speed channel and signal integrity characterization following degree completion. · Direct ownership of a characterization program whose results became datasheet limits or qualification thresholds for a shipping product. · Strong VNA measurement experience to 50 GHz or beyond, including de-embedding, mixed-mode S-parameters (Sdd/Scc/Scd/Sdc) and insertion/return-loss mask interpretation. · Hands-on TX/RX SerDes characterization, jitter decomposition, BER bathtubs, PVT shmoos and equalization/adaptation analysis. · Demonstrated common-mode and mode-conversion measurement depth, with the ability to distinguish channel behavior from fixture and calibration artifacts. · Statistical characterization and guard-band derivation across corners, with clear treatment of measurement uncertainty, sample size and aging. · Experience with VNAs, oscilloscopes of at least 50 GHz bandwidth, BERTs, jitter instrumentation, thermal forcing and ATE characterization load boards. · BS in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, with the technical communication and coordination skills to hand off defensible limits to validation and manufacturing teams. Essential Experience · Characterization leadership for shipping 100G/lane or 200G/lane retimers, PHYs, AECs or AOCs. · Deep mixed-mode characterization where common-mode behavior affects information transport and link margin. · Experience producing datasheet limits that a separate validation team independently qualified. · Multi-carrier or proprietary coding schemes, including OFDM-style subcarriers and space-time coding, and their characterization implications. · Published work or patents in channel modeling, de-embedding or SerDes characterization. · MS or PhD with a concentration in communications, RF/microwave engineering or signal integrity. If this is the role you have been looking for and you want to be part of a growing Company, with an exciting future then we would love to hear from you. Together We Kandou It!! title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
description: About Orakl Oncology At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities. Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology. About the Role We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions. You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators. This is a hands-on scientific leadership role . You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme. You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions. The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work. What You'll Do Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve. Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality. Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses. Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims. Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes. Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations. Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks. Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications. Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations. Minimum Qualifications PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology. Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings. Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors , including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions. A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health , with clear intellectual and analytical contributions. Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures. Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations. Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English , including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers. Preferred Qualifications Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning. Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow. Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints. Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling. Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners. Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements. Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network. Who You Are A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time. A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems. Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly. Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods. An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress. Why Join Orakl Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions. Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together. Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data. Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions. Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme. Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support. Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme. Interview Process HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions. description: Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain . Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif. L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain. À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École. Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques. Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret. Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité. Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins. L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité. 🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’ industrie du futur. Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ? 🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600). Ce recrutement est au cœur de la stratégie d’innovation de Mines Saint-Etienne pour permettre à un brevet IMT de se concrétiser en une technologie permettant de capter le CO2 des fumées industrielles, et de contribuer ainsi à l’atteinte de l’objectif Français de Neutralité carbone · Vous assurez le développement d’un pilote de captage du CO2, · Vous participez au transfert de technologie entre une méthodologie brevetée et la spin-off Carbon Cage, · Vous contribuez à un enjeu majeur de notre société, · Vous rendez compte l’équipe GasHyDyn qui soutient les développements méthodologiques, et vous interagissez au quotidien avec sa spin-off Carbon Cage. title: Senior Distributed Systems Engineer - Cache
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3>About Us</h3> <p>At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.</p> <p>At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.</p></div><p><strong>Available Locations: Atlanta, GA, Austin, TX, Champaign, IL, New York, NY, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Washington, DC</strong></p> <h2>About the Department</h2> <p>Cloudflare's Engineering Team builds and runs the software that helps power millions of Internet properties. Product development covers both new features and functionality as well as scaling our existing software to meet the challenges of a massively growing customer base.</p> <p>The Content Delivery group helps make the Internet faster, safer, and more reliable by building and optimizing one of the world's largest CDNs.</p> <h2>Role Summary</h2> <p>The Cache team builds and operates the high-performance reverse proxy and caching data plane at Cloudflare's edge. Built on Pingora, Cloudflare's open-source Rust framework for fast, reliable network services, this software serves cached content, routes traffic across cache tiers, and connects Cloudflare to customer origins. Its performance, correctness, and resilience directly affect request latency, origin load, and availability across Cloudflare's global network.</p> <p>You will work primarily on the reverse proxy and the services that support it: backend routing and load balancing, cache storage and indexing, globally distributed purge, Tiered Cache routing, and production observability. These systems are also foundational building blocks for teams across Cloudflare, which use the proxy, caching, routing, and purge capabilities to power their own products. The team carries these capabilities through shared internal interfaces, distributed control planes, and customer-facing products including Cache Rules, Tiered Cache, Cache Reserve, Workers Cache API, and Always Online. Features ship end to end: you will help design, implement, test, roll out, and operate the systems you build.</p> <p>This is a good fit if you enjoy problems where latency, correctness, and reliability are hard requirements; where changes must be introduced safely across a global fleet; and where improvements can benefit a significant portion of Internet traffic.</p> <h2>Role Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Design, build, and operate the high-performance cache and proxy data plane that serves content at Cloudflare's edge and connects to customer origins</li> <li>Contribute to Pingora and the production services built on it, improving asynchronous I/O, connection handling, memory and disk efficiency, and tail latency</li> <li>Improve cache correctness and performance through object placement, retention, admission and eviction policies, range-request handling, and resilience to corrupt or incomplete data</li> <li>Build globally distributed purge and Tiered Cache systems that invalidate content quickly, select efficient cache paths, improve hit rates, and reduce origin load</li> <li>Deliver shared platform capabilities and customer-facing APIs and rules for cache keys, TTLs, response handling, purge behavior, and programmatic access from Workers</li> <li>Own features end to end: write technical designs, implement services and libraries, add automated tests and observability, drive staged rollouts, and operate the resulting systems in production</li> <li>Participate in the team's on-call rotation, lead incident response and post-mortems, and continually improve reliability, capacity, and operational tooling</li> <li>Reason carefully about failure modes and blast radius, using traffic cohorts, measurable guardrails, and rollback mechanisms to introduce high-impact changes safely</li> <li>Partner with product and engineering teams across Cloudflare that depend on or extend the cache and proxy platform</li> <li>Raise the engineering bar through code review, mentorship, clear written communication, and improvements to team standards and tooling</li> </ul> <h2>Role Requirements (Must-Have Skills)</h2> <ul> <li>Minimum 4 years of professional experience designing, building, and operating production software systems</li> <li>Strong proficiency in at least one systems or backend language such as Rust, Go, C, or C++, with a willingness to work in Rust</li> <li>Strong understanding of HTTP semantics and transport protocols such as TCP, TLS, and QUIC</li> <li>Experience designing and implementing secure, resilient, high-performance distributed systems</li> <li>Experience with Linux systems, networking, concurrency, and performance analysis</li> <li>Track record of production ownership, including monitoring, debugging, on-call, incident response, and ongoing reliability improvements</li> <li>Experience using metrics, logs, traces, profiling, and experiments to understand production behavior and validate improvements</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to write clear technical designs and lead projects across team boundaries</li> <li>Willingness to use AI-assisted engineering tools to accelerate development and investigation while remaining accountable for correctness, security, and design quality</li> </ul> <h2>Nice-to-Have Skills</h2> <ul> <li>Professional experience with Rust or high-performance asynchronous systems</li> <li>Experience with caches, HTTP proxies, CDNs, distributed storage, or latency-sensitive data-plane services</li> <li>Experience analyzing memory use, disk I/O, resource contention, and tail latency in production systems</li> <li>Experience building APIs or distributed control planes using event streaming, relational databases, or analytical data systems</li> <li>Familiarity with Kubernetes, Kafka, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, or similar infrastructure</li> <li>Experience contributing to open-source software or leading multi-team engineering programs</li> </ul> <p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location and level.</p> <p>San Francisco Estimated Base salary $194,000 - $266,000.</p> <p>Seattle, Washington D.C., New York Estimated Base salary $185,000 - $254,000.</p> <p>Austin, Illinois, Atlanta Estimated Base salary $168,000 - $231,000.</p> title: People Business Partner Lead, EMEA
description: ClickHouse is hiring an EMEA People Business Partner Lead to be the primary strategic People partner to business leaders across the region. By combining deep business partnership, organizational insight, and proactive People strategy, this role will help shape how the EMEA organization evolves—not simply respond to the needs of the business as they arise. This role is responsible for deeply understanding the business, its growth strategy, and the unique dynamics across EMEA, and translating that understanding into proactive People and organizational strategy. You will help leaders anticipate needs, spot risks and opportunities, and build the teams, leadership capability, and practices required to scale. In this role, you will help leaders anticipate organizational needs and identify risks and opportunities, while enabling them with the leadership capability and people practices needed to scale their teams successfully. Success in this role requires strong business acumen, organizational judgment, and the ability to move beyond responding to leadership requests to independently identifying what the business needs. Because EMEA is a diverse and complex region, this person must be able to understand the different business and market dynamics across countries while maintaining a cohesive view of the region and its long-term organizational needs. What You’ll Do Strategic People & Business Partnership Serve as the primary People partner to our managers and leaders based in EMEA, deeply understanding their growth strategy, operating model, and organizational dynamics. Translate business priorities into proactive People and organizational strategies, bringing an independent point of view and identifying risks and opportunities early. Partner with leaders on complex organizational decisions and ensure People is embedded early in business planning. Organizational Strategy & Effectiveness Partner with EMEA leadership on organizational design, workforce planning, role clarity, team effectiveness, and leadership capability. Identify patterns and systemic issues across teams and translate insights into recommendations and action. Use workforce, talent, and organizational data to inform performance, talent, succession, and organizational decisions. People Strategy & Program Leadership Partner with global People teams to adapt programs for regional needs and identify gaps or opportunities for improvement. Drive adoption and effectiveness of People initiatives, bringing regional insights back to the global People organization. Global Partnership & Influence Serve as the strategic People partner to leaders navigating complex employee and organizational situations across EMEA. Partner with People Operations and Legal to navigate performance, conduct, organizational change, and other complex people matters. Identify patterns and proactively address broader organizational or leadership issues. Bridge EMEA leadership and the global People organization, ensuring regional needs inform company-wide People strategy. Partner across People, Finance, Recruiting, Compensation, Legal, and other functions to align organizational and talent priorities with business needs. title: Strategic Project Manager
description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. Location This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region. Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp. Your Mission You get customers live. Hands on, end to end, and fast. As a Senior Project Manager , you make large, global blp transformations happen. These programs touch finance, procurement and supply chain at once, run across multiple ERP systems and legal entities, and roll out country by country. Your job is to orchestrate all of it and get the customer live: the first go-live above all, because that is where credibility is won or lost, and then wave after wave with the same discipline. You run the steering committee, you lead a blp team on each engagement, and you do that across several engagements at once. At both levels, scope is the single biggest lever on whether a project goes live on time. Protecting it is a daily job, not a contract clause. You escalate early and precisely rather than absorbing problems until they become critical. You will not be alone with the technical side. Integrations Engineers handle the connection into the ERP, Technical Project Managers handle the harder solution design, and our Consultants take over the automation work after go-live. On our largest strategic accounts a Client Partner carries the relationship and the commercial number, so your attention goes to delivery quality. We have done this many times, so you are not inventing the approach each time. A proven onboarding method and a strong toolkit are what let you carry your own customers from early on. Your Career Path in Project Management This is the path most of our delivery leadership came through, and we hire at every step of it. We place you according to your experience and the size of the programs you have delivered, and we are explicit about what the next step requires. Project Manager: You get customers live end to end, several in parallel: guided onboarding for commercial customers, leading enterprise projects yourself, or a workstream on our largest programs. Typically you bring 2+ years in consulting, implementation or project management. Senior Project Manager: You make large, global transformations happen: multiple ERPs, entities and countries, the steering committee, and a blp team on each engagement. Typically you bring 5+ years delivering complex, multi-country programs. Next steps: Lead a delivery team, or move into Consulting and from there towards our Client Partner role on strategic accounts. Moves into Consulting or Customer Success Engineering are open at every level, and many of our people make them. Key Responsibilities Run implementations end to end: kick-off, scope, planning, configuration, testing and go-live. Manage several customers in parallel at different stages, and keep every one of them on date. Work with customers on their processes, and flag early where a process assumption will not hold. Coordinate the specialists on your projects: Integrations Engineers, Technical Project Managers and AI Automation Specialists. Own scope actively. Recognize a change request for what it is and handle it deliberately. Keep the project inside its budget, and raise it early when the effort is drifting. Hand over cleanly at go-live to our Consultants and support organization. In addition, as a Senior Project Manager Own the delivery outcome of global programs from kick-off to the last go-live: plan, scope, dependencies and date. Drive the first go-live relentlessly, then run wave planning across ERPs, entities and countries. Run the steering committee and own the decisions that come out of it. Write and execute the recovery plan when a program is off track. Lead the blp team on each engagement and coach the Project Managers working on your programs. What We're Really Looking For The following key attributes ensure success in this role: Scope Discipline – You notice when a project is quietly growing, and you raise it rather than absorbing it. Ownership & Autonomy – You take initiative, move things forward, and deliver end to end without being chased. Escalation Judgment – You escalate early, to the right person, with a proposal rather than a problem. Client Confidence – You are comfortable running a meeting with a customer's finance or IT lead in it. Four-Language Fluency – Technology, process, data and people. You speak each well enough to spot where a roadblock really sits. Structured Under Pressure – When a project goes sideways you get sharper and more organized, not louder. What You Bring 5+ years of experience delivering complex projects: management consulting, enterprise software implementation, or large-scale transformation delivery. Proven track record running multi-country or multi-entity programs with senior client stakeholders, and steering a committee that includes client executives. Experience leading a delivery team rather than only a plan. Strong analytical and communication skills. You can translate a business need into something a technical team can act on. Fluent in German and English, spoken and written. Bonus points for ERP implementation experience, finance or supply chain processes, or AI-driven SaaS. Benefits High ownership environment – you shape your projects, outcomes, and career path. Impact at scale – your work powers automation across global enterprises. Cross-functional exposure – work with engineers, data scientists, and business leaders daily. Real growth – fast-paced environment, steep learning curve, and structured career progression. Employee ownership – be part of a majority employee-owned company with a best-in-class stock option program. Amazing team – become part of a driven and collaborative group of innovators. Technology exposure – be at the forefront of AI and enjoy continuous learning opportunities. Visits & offsites – paid visits and stays at our HQ in Zurich, including collaborative team offsites. Ready to build the future of ERP automation? Join us and own your impact. Learn more about blp and our values at https://blp.digital/company/careers . Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Forward Deployed Engineer (all genders) - Remote Germany or Hungary
description: About Linro Linro is a Berlin-based cloud security company building a real-time, agentic cloud-security platform. Teams ship with AI. AI ships with Linro. Infrastructure changes constantly, and increasingly it's AI agents making the changes. Tools that scan snapshots and flag risk after the fact can't keep up. Linro enforces intended state across the whole lifecycle instead, from commit to runtime: MCP and pre-commit hooks at commit time, blast-radius simulation that blocks bad changes before they ship, and real-time detection, enforcement and auto-remediation in production. Most tools tell you what's wrong. Linro stops it. We have each been on the receiving end of this problem: Running cloud security at scale, building the platforms underneath it, and shipping in regulated systems where a wrong change isn't an option. Founded in Berlin in 2026 and built fully remote across Europe, Linro has a platform that's real and working, with plenty still to shape. The role You would be the engineer who gets Linro running inside a customer's real environment and keeps it running. Our founders and go-to-market team win the customer and own the commercial relationship. You own the technical side: you take a customer from signed agreement to a working install and the first blocked change, and stay on it after go-live for upgrades, incidents and tuning. Part of this happens on-site: you may spend a few days at a customer's office to get an install running or to work through a problem with their team. Everything you learn goes back to engineering and product. This is an engineering role, not a support or sales role, and there is no quota. What you will do Run customer onboarding end to end: connect the customer's cloud accounts, whichever provider they run on, deploy sensors (managed, or inside the customer's own cluster) and get to a first blocked change fast. Write and tune SQL-based policies and policy packs mapped to each customer's frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIS2, DORA), and keep false positives low. Wire Linro guardrails into the customer's Terraform and CI/CD workflows and into their AI coding agents through MCP. Run Linro in production at the customer: monitor, upgrade and respond when it breaks. Debug inside their environment, hand reproducible findings to engineering, and fix what you can yourself. Close the loop: structured feedback to product and engineering, reusable playbooks for the next customer, and a seat in scoping calls so that what we promise is what installs. What we are looking for 5 to 6+ years of customer-facing technical delivery (forward deployed or solutions engineering, SRE or platform consulting), deploying infrastructure or security software in customer environments and keeping it running afterwards. Hands-on cloud experience: you have run real workloads, identity and access, networking and audit logging on at least one major cloud, and you pick up the others quickly. You are a solid engineer. You write real code in Go or Python for integrations and tooling, read Go services, and are comfortable with SQL and APIs. You use AI coding agents daily, such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and have hands-on MCP experience. You understand how companies work: change management, approvals, release and audit processes, and how to fit Linro into them. Restricted-network experience: proxies, private networking, data residency, self-hosted or in-cluster installs. Communication and comfort with ambiguity. You explain trade-offs clearly to engineers and executives, set honest expectations, and keep making progress when requirements are still unclear. Fluent English. Open to travel. To customers across Europe and the US, up to roughly a quarter of your time. Nice to have Turning compliance frameworks (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001) into concrete controls. Policy-as-code (OPA/Rego, Sentinel, Cedar) or CSPM tooling. How we work We work remotely across Europe. We get the whole team together in person somewhere in Europe once a quarter for a few days. We work async by default, write things down, and protect people's focus time. What we offer Real ownership. You own every customer deployment from day one, with direct access to the founders and to the engineers who built what you are deploying. Meaningful equity. You are an early employee, and your stake reflects it. Competitive salary, benchmarked to the market. A quarterly European offsite, and a team that takes both the mission and each other's time seriously. The honest version This is early. You will often be the first person to run Linro in a customer's environment, and you will write the playbooks as you go. If you want a polished onboarding process and a stable product surface, this is not it. If you want to sit between a new category and the customers who need it, and you like the idea of deploying the thing that keeps AI agents from breaking production, we should talk. title: Embedded System Lead Engineer
description: Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer. Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats. France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service. Pelagon is backed by Hexa , the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised. The role As Embedded System Lead Engineer , you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it. What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget. You will lead their technical development , from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come. These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge , on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role. The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it. What you'll own Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications. The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt. Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS). The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment. Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore. Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench. Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units. The hard problems you'll be solving These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point: Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling. Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell. Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible. Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it. Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean. Who we're looking for You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically: 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world. Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems . This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space. Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack : electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal. Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control. Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do. A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters. Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it. Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale. Why join now Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that. A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space. Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years. AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about. A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it. title: Senior Backend Developer (Python, Java)
description: Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we've been building that knowledge for over 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we're also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax advisors don't just get an answer, but an answer they're willing to attach their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it daily, generating over 100 million euros in ARR across Europe. We're looking for a Senior Backend Developer to help build that. HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD Our Knowledge Team is the layer between the content and the AI. We pull in millions of documents from internal databases, public sources, and the web, standardize them, and make them usable for the AI agents that distill answers from them. The real challenge isn't storage but selection. Out of those millions of documents, exactly one paragraph needs to surface the moment a lawyer asks a question. Surface the wrong one, and the agent gives an answer that sounds plausible but is wrong. In our field, that's not a bug: it's a liability issue. What you build determines whether the answer holds up. There's work to be done, and it's the kind of work you could talk about for a whole evening. The pipeline has been running for six years, built in Scala and Java, and parts of it deserve a new foundation. Reranking is the biggest need: determining which passage, out of a mountain of legal documents, actually answers the question being asked. Not just which one contains the matching words. That's the problem we’re solving. The team is strong on the scientific side, in retrieval, and in understanding what a model can and can't handle. What we're looking to add is engineering firepower: someone who can turn ideas into systems that deliver. Not to rebuild everything over six months just because it was once set up differently, but to see where the real gains are and start there. You build and improve the pipeline that turns content into knowledge our AI agents can use. You work on reranking quality, so the agent gets the right information, not just the most information. You help shape the approach to retrieval and knowledge extraction, bringing in what you've seen work elsewhere. You work in Python for everything new, and in Java where the existing codebase calls for it. You make technical decisions, even when no one is looking over your shoulder. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR You're an engineer who looks beyond the ticket. You want to understand why something is being built and what it delivers for the customer, and you're not afraid to have an opinion about it. You don't need a manager to make a technical call, and you speak up when you think something should be done differently. Experience with Python and Java. Everything newly built is developed in Python, closely aligned with the AI teams who also work in it. But a large part of our current codebase runs on Java, so you need to be comfortable working with that too. Experience with Elasticsearch. That's where it's determined which information the agent gets to see. Experience with Scala or Kotlin is a plus. The ingestion layer runs largely on Scala. You come from SaaS, a product-driven organization, or a scale-up, and you thrive on autonomy rather than oversight. WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR At Lefebvre Sdu, you'll work in an organization that's in the middle of a transformation and takes the public market seriously. That's the direction, and we're making the journey together. You'll get the mandate, the space, and the colleagues to make it happen. You'll join a team with a Product Owner, three frontend developers, a UX designer, and a Scrum Master who also works across multiple teams. You'll have room to shape your role and help determine how we work, with a clear shared goal: building the AI-first platform. You'll bring the backend experience the team needs to take real end-to-end ownership, and you'll report to the Lead Frontend Developer. You'll take part in the team's regular scrum rituals (dailies, refinements, retros, planning) and have one-on-ones with your manager. Through the team, you'll also be an important point of contact for application administrators and customer support who need technical assistance, so you should enjoy breaking down technical problems and communicating about them with less technical colleagues. A place where you have influence from day one: on the approach, the processes, and the direction. Colleagues who deliberately chose Lefebvre Sdu over big tech jobs because here, they're building something that doesn't exist yet. Base salary between €5,500 and €6,450 per month, based on a 36-hour week, since that's full-time for us. Plus a lot of extra allowances (see below). A bonus tied to company performance: a fixed year-end bonus of 4% and profit sharing of up to 6%. 23 vacation days and a personal choice budget of 12%, of which 8% is holiday pay and 4% is freely allocable. Want more vacation? Just buy it. A bonus of up to 10% of your salary, based on company performance and individual performance. A solid pension plan through PGB, including supplementary partner insurance. Collective insurance plans. A travel allowance of €0.25 per kilometer or a public transport reimbursement, plus an attractive bike plan. For employees with a commute of less than 10 km or more than 60 km, we have an adjusted arrangement. Two days a week in the office in The Hague, within walking distance of Voorburg station. The rest of the week, wherever you work best. Room to grow: in your craft, in your role, in the organization. WANT TO KNOW MORE? We'd love to tell you all about the team and the role. Send us your CV and you'll hear from us within a few business days. Have a few questions first? Message or call Elize at 0641186590. title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description: Legal AI is zo goed als de kennis erachter, en aan die kennis bouwen we bij Lefebvre Sdu al 200 jaar. Dag in, dag uit. Wet voor wet. Woord voor woord. Dat doen we zo zorgvuldig dat andere legal AI-tools op onze data en software draaien. Onze developers willen snel bouwen en veilig live gaan, zonder uren kwijt te zijn aan pipelines en repository-setup. Daar zorg jij voor. Onze infrastructuur draait op AWS, met Kubernetes via EKS, Terraform en Helm, en onze CI/CD loopt via GitHub Actions. In die pipelines borg jij bij elke release de secure coding-eisen van ISO 27001, van SAST en security scanning tot code quality checks en de OWASP Top 10. Je wordt het eerste aanspreekpunt voor de developers in Product & Technology, brengt structuur in hoe het team werkt en bouwt mee aan de volgende stappen, zoals de overstap van Helm naar ArgoCD. Je weet dat het gelukt is als de andere teams merkbaar minder tijd kwijt zijn aan hun deployments, de infrastructuur gezond is en je precies ziet wat er gebeurt. Wat nu nog ontbreekt, is het team dat dit zelf gaat dragen, en dat bouw jij mee op. DIT ZOEKEN WIJ Je bent een DevOps engineer die het liefst dicht bij de developers zit. Je bouwt een platform waar anderen zelf mee verder kunnen, vindt het vanzelfsprekend dat security in elke pipeline is ingebouwd en brengt graag rust en overzicht in een omgeving die in beweging is. Je zorgt voor duidelijkheid in technische processen en afspraken. Ervaring met het bouwen en doorontwikkelen van een softwareproduct is een pré.
